summary: Sandra Bell is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University by 1991 and held a post there.
Sandra Hochwarter works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her Mag.phil. at the University of Vienna, where she was supervised by Klaus-Dieter Mathes and taught by Anne MacDonald.
Sang-Kyun Sun is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Delhi under Sanghasen Singh and served as a lecturer at JinGak Sangha College (attested 1995).

Sangay Dorji is a scholar in Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tengtho Monastery and the Institute of Language and Culture Studies, taught at Simtokha Dzong, and served as Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission (attested 1999–2004).

Sangharakshita (1925–2018) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and under teachers including Jagdish Kashyap, Dhardo Rinpoche, Jianmin Chen, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dudjom Rinpoche, and founded the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1967.

Sangseraima Ujeed (b. 1988) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2014–2019) and held a Ho postdoctoral fellowship at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~2019–2021).

Historian Sanjay Subrahmanyam (b. 1961) studied at Delhi School of Economics and the University of Delhi. His posts include Oxford (1993–1995, 2002), EHESS (1995–2002), UCLA (founding director 2005–2011, endowed chair 2014), and Collège de France (2013).
Sanjaya Lall (1940–2005) studied at St. Xavier's High School in Patna and St John's College, Oxford (~1960–1965), and held a post at the University of Oxford from around 1979 to 2005.
Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under teacher Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya (attested 1994) and traditional teacher A. P. Lama.

Sanjukta Gupta (b. 1931) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She earned a Ph.D. from Visva-Bharati and a D.Lett. from Utrecht under Jan Gonda, and held posts at Jadavpur, Utrecht, and Oxford.
Sanne Dokter-Mersch (b. 1989) is an Indology scholar who earned her PhD at Leiden University (~2016–2021), where she was supervised by Peter C. Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi.

Sao Htun Hmat Win was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard University and under Bhaddanta Narada. He held posts at the University of Rangoon, the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and Myanmar's Ministry of Religious Affairs (attested 2002).

Saphalya Amatya is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Chief Exploration Officer at the Department of Archaeology (attested 1974) and as editor of Ancient Nepal (attested 1987).

Sara L. McClintock specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. After earning her PhD from Harvard (2002), she held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2003) and Emory University as associate professor of religion.
Sarah Aoife Richardson is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who completed her PhD at the University of Toronto in 2016 under Jenny Purtle.

Sarah E. Fraser works in history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Michigan and Kobe University, and held posts at Northwestern University (from 1996) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2000).

Sarah H. Jacoby is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Yale (~1991–1995) and the University of Virginia (~1999–2007), and held posts at Columbia University (2006–2009) and Northwestern University (starting 2009).

Sarah Harding (b. 1951) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Drubpön Lama Tenpa, taught at Naropa University (~1992–2018), and became a fellow at the Tsadra Foundation (~2000).

Sarah J. Horton specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein and served as an assistant professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).

Sarah Shaw is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Lance S. Cousins. She holds affiliations with Oxford's Faculty of Oriental Studies, Wolfson College, and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (attested 2013).
